entities.name: Delayed-onset muscle soreness
observations: Exercise-induced muscle soreness and transient functional impairment, commonly studied after eccentric exercise.

entities.name: PMID:40784513
observations: Meta-analysis of 10 RCTs (299 participants): HBOT did not significantly reduce exercise-induced muscle soreness overall (95% CI −0.91 to 0.48; P=.54).
Reported a pooled improvement in measures of exercise-induced muscle injury/recovery, but the abstract describes heterogeneous outcomes and subgroup soreness results were inconsistent.

entities.name: PMID:10730995
observations: Randomized placebo-controlled study of 24 healthy men found no difference in recovery of strength, soreness, or arm circumference after seven HBOT/placebo sessions following eccentric exercise.

entities.name: PMID:12964857
observations: Controlled study (16 university volunteers) found five HBOT sessions did not improve soreness, strength, power, fatigue, circumference, or creatine kinase versus untreated control; authors concluded recovery was not accelerated.

entities.name: PMID:10496576
observations: Randomized controlled study of 66 untrained men found no significant group differences in pain; some treatment groups showed greater recovery of eccentric torque than sham.
